summary: The first IOAI brought school teams to Burgas for Scientific and Practical rounds. Scientific work combined at-home preparation and on-site model-building; the Practical round used existing AI tools for creative tasks.
structure: Scientific round has at-home and on-site tasks. Practical round is separate. Do not relabel at-home work as a national qualification round.

summary: Kazakhstan’s first Republican AI Olymp brought school students to Astana IT University. The organizer reports 40 finalists; the authoritative organizer-supplied final table contains 38 entries, including all highlighted rows. Remote-stage and two contest-day scores are retained. Missing entries and medals are not inferred.
structure: Qualification, a homework Kaggle competition, then two in-person contest days in Astana. Results supported national training-camp selection. May 3–5 is the owner-reported 2025 programme window, not independently verified contest dates; the May 5 recap timestamp is not an event schedule.

statistics.population: 40 finalists reported by the organizer; the supplied final table has 38 entries, not a reconstructed 40-person roster
statistics.method: Organizer recap; no medals inferred from screenshot colours.

statistics.population: All 38 supplied entries, including highlighted red rows; not all 40 announced finalists
statistics.method: Organizer original reconciled cell-by-cell; public recap provides attribution, not a downloadable score file.

summary: The Republican AI Olymp final took place at Astana IT University on April 11–12, 2026. Forty students qualified; the authoritative organizer-supplied final table contains 39 entries. All 23 published awardees are matched by name to this table: 3 Gold, 5 Silver and 15 Bronze.
structure: Online selection followed by two final contest rounds: one task on April 11 and two on April 12. Twelve students were invited to a training camp, from which eight would form the national team. The 39-row table is the authoritative provided version, not a claim that all 40 qualifiers are listed. Qualification standings are not supplied.

statistics.population: 40 qualified students reported by the federation; not the number of rows in the supplied workbook
statistics.method: Federation recap; qualifiers are distinct from supplied-table entries.

statistics.population: 39 supplied entries, including all 23 named medal recipients. Rates describe this table only, not all 40 qualifiers
statistics.method: Public organizer award list explicitly matched by name to original workbook; never inferred from rank or ties.

summary: Fizmat AI Olympiad offers school teams a practical introduction to machine learning and data analysis. Its 2025 edition had a qualification round and a two-day Almaty final; the official archive links final results and task collections.
structure: September 28 online qualification, October 30–31 Almaty final; season range is not continuous contest duration. Final problem 1–5 columns belong to one final team table.

summary: Fizmat AI Olympiad is organized by the National School of Physics and Math. September qualification precedes two five-hour final rounds on October 27–28 at SDU University, Kaskelen. October 26–30 includes travel. Final results are not available as of October 23.
structure: September 20 online qualification: five tasks, four hours, teams of 1–3. The organizer reports 578 entering teams and approximately 1,500 students from 28 countries. The separate post-jury qualification table has 410 ranked teams from 25 countries. These are different populations. The final page now names SDU University, Kaskelen, although its heading and older press report still say Almaty. Arrival October 26, contest October 27–28, closing October 29, departure October 30. Published award quotas are not actual medals. Consult current eligibility rules: the press release inconsistently says grades 8–12 and 9–12.

statistics.population: Teams reported by the organizer immediately after the qualifying round; not the post-jury ranking
statistics.method: Explicit organizer report. Approximately 1,500 students is not an exact individual count; no medals inferred.

statistics.population: Ranked teams after the September 22 jury decision; not all entrants and not final contestants
statistics.method: Counted the official page's 410 DATA records and 25 country labels; five original task-score columns sum to displayed totals. No named rows copied or awards inferred.

results.label: Qualification results
results.coverage: Qualification only. The October 27–28 final has not taken place.

summary: Northern Eurasia OAI is an individual, practical AI olympiad with distributed international participation. structure: Dedicated edition May 3–4, hybrid. Homework examples are explicitly practice, not evidence for a published qualification ranking. Russia is organizer context, not all participant locations; approved Central University mapping is retained, city absent.
